QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_28

question.text: What is the concept of 'convexity' in bond valuation?

answer.text: A measure of the curvature in the relationship between bond prices and yields, indicating that duration alone can misestimate price changes for large yield movements and that a convexity adjustment improves the approximation
The tendency of bond prices to move in a straight line when yields change
The credit risk premium added to the risk-free rate for corporate bonds
The time value component of a bond option's premium

explanation.text: The Logic: Convexity captures the curvature of the price/yield relationship for a bond. Duration gives a straight-line approximation of price change for a yield move; because the true relationship is curved, duration underestimates the price change when yields fall and overestimates the price change when yields rise. Adding a convexity adjustment improves the approximation for large yield moves. The Trap: The price/yield relationship is not linear, which is exactly why convexity exists. Convexity is a price-sensitivity measure, not a credit-risk concept or an option premium component. Note: Bonds with higher convexity tend to behave more favourably than duration alone would predict when yields fall, while the overestimation issue applies on the upside in yields.
